summary: Susan Neiman is a philosopher who studied at the Free University of Berlin and Harvard University (Ph.D.). She held professorships at Yale (1989–1996) and Tel Aviv University (1996–2000), and has served as Director of the Einstein Forum since 2000.
Susan Niditch is a religious studies scholar. She served as a faculty member in the religion department at Amherst College from circa 1978 to 2020.

Susanne Hoeber Rudolph (1930–2015) was a scholar of Indology and political science. She studied at Sarah Lawrence College, Harvard University, and Radcliffe College, later teaching at Harvard (~1955–1963) and serving as professor at the University of Chicago from 1964.

Susanne Mrozik is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned an M.T.S. at Harvard University, studying under Charles Hallisey, Diana L. Eck, Stephanie W. Jamison, and Margaret R. Miles. She held posts at Western Michigan University and Mount Holyoke College.

Sushil Kumar De was an Indologist educated at Presidency College, Chennai, the University of Calcutta, SOAS, and the University of Bonn. He held academic posts at Presidency College, the University of Calcutta, the University of Dhaka (1923–1947), and Jadavpur University (~1956–1960).

Susumu Otake is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at the University of Tsukuba under Makio Takemura. He has held part-time lecturer positions at Kyoto University, Hanazono University, and Bukkyo University.

Susumu Shimazono is a religious studies and Japanology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and UC Berkeley. He served as professor of religious studies at the University of Tokyo (1995–2013) and later held posts at Sophia University.

Susumu Yamaguchi (1895–1976) was a Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Otani University, under Sylvain Lévi and Louis de La Vallée Poussin, and at Kyoto University. He taught at Otani University (1924–1964) and Kyoto Sangyo University.

Suwanda H. J. Sugunasiri is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Nalanda College, the University of London, the University of Pennsylvania, and the University of Toronto. He founded and served as president of Nalanda College of Buddhist Studies.

Suzanne Karpelès (1890–1968) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at EPHE under Sylvain Lévi, Alfred Foucher, and Louis Finot. She served at EFEO (1922–1941), the National Library of Cambodia, and the Buddhist Institute.

Suzanne Newcombe is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who earned her doctorate at the University of Cambridge. She has held posts at Cambridge, the London School of Economics, Inform, King's College London, and the Open University.

Sven Hedin (1865–1952) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Stockholm University, Uppsala University, the Humboldt University of Berlin, and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg.
Sven Wittemann is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts degree at the International Buddhist College under the supervision of Kapila Abhayawansa.

Swami Dayananda Saraswati (1930–2015) was a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at Bangalore Sanskrit College and under teachers including Chinmayananda Saraswati, Swami Tapovan Maharaj, Swami Pranavananda, Swami Tarananda Giri, P. S. Subramania Iyer, and Veeraraghavachariar.

Swami Lakshman Joo (1907–1991) was an Indologist, philosopher, and religious studies scholar who studied under Maheshwar Nath Razdan from 1926 to 1933. He later founded the Universal Shaiva Fellowship in 1991.
Swami Satyananda Puri (1902–1942) was a scholar in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at and held a post at the University of Calcutta.

Swami Sivananda Saraswati (1887–1963) was a scholar in religious studies, philosophy, and Indology who studied at Thanjavur Medical College. He founded the Divine Life Society in 1936 and the Yoga-Vedanta Forest Academy in 1948.
Swami Vimalananda (1872–1908) was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Ripon College and became a disciple of Swami Vivekananda in 1897.

Swami Vivekananda (1863–1902) was a philosopher, religious studies, and Indology scholar. He studied at Presidency University, Scottish Church College, and the University of Calcutta, and was a disciple of Ramakrishna between circa 1881 and 1886.

Sydney Frank Markham (1897–1975) was a historian and archaeologist who studied at Wadham College from circa 1920 to 1923. He served as Secretary and later President of the Museums Association between circa 1929 and 1942.
